subject: Procurement guidance: marketplace vs direct for regulated fintech purchase
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@acme-fin.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme-fin.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Redwood procurement path — marketplace vs direct

Hi Priyom,

We're kicking off procurement for the ML inference platform at Acme Financial (regulated payments). Procurement has asked us to evaluate whether to purchase via AWS Marketplace or pursue a direct commercial contract with Redwood. Key constraints:
- Need SOC 2 evidence & DPIA language in contract
- Prefer automated invoicing and PO processing
- Data residency may require EU-only tenants for some services (we're US but some data routes go to EU)
- Timeline: procurement wants an approvable route in ~3 weeks

Can you advise on pros/cons for marketplace vs direct, and whether Redwood supports a co-sell flow via AWS (we'd be using AWS infra)? Any docs or pricing worksheets you can share would be very helpful.

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Platform Security
Acme Financial

Attachment: procurement-questions.pdf (reference)

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@acme-fin.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood procurement path — marketplace vs direct

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear summary.

Short answer up front:
- Marketplace (AWS Marketplace) = faster procurement, single-click subscription, automated invoicing via AWS; good when you need quick onboarding and standard terms.
- Direct contract = better for custom SLAs, DPA/DPIA revisions, committed capacity (Dedicated), and certain enterprise billing needs; takes longer due to legal and procurement reviews.

Notes specific to Acme's constraints:
- SOC 2: we can provide the SOC 2 report and control narratives (I attached a SOC2 excerpt). Marketplace purchases do not prevent us from providing evidence; we just operate under our standard SOC2 coverage.
- DPIA/DPA: For legal edits or special data-processing clauses, a direct contract is more flexible. Marketplace contracts are generally standard; if procurement needs custom language, direct is the route.
- Invoicing/POs: AWS Marketplace bills through AWS (good if you want consolidated vendor management). For PO-driven invoicing directly to Acme, direct contract is preferable.
- Co-sell via AWS: we do participate in co-sell motions with AWS for certain deals — that can help with procurement lift, especially when AWS engages your procurement team.

I'll loop in our GTM and legal leads to outline recommended next steps and timelines. For now, attached is a pricing worksheet and a short comparison table.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-pricing-worksheet.xlsx

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:17:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood procurement path — marketplace vs direct

Priyom — quick internal notes before we reply to Acme:

1) If the customer needs an EU-only tenant for certain data, we should propose a hybrid: sign via Marketplace for quick onboarding for non-sensitive workloads and run regulated workloads on a Dedicated/Private deployment (direct contract) — this splits procurement so they get immediate value while we negotiate the enterprise DPA.
2) Co-sell: confirm whether the AWS account team will attach a co-sell SKU; if so, we can surface AWS incentives. Marcus, can you confirm whether the deal qualifies for co-sell and if we have a managed licensing SKU? If not, we'll default to standard Marketplace listing + direct commitment for Dedicated.
3) Pricing: for mid-size usage, marketplace list prices can be slightly higher; contracted discounts apply for Direct with reserved capacity.
4) Timeline: if procurement needs approval in 3 weeks, Marketplace gets them across the finish line fastest.

I'll draft a short note for Elena summarizing those options and the recommended staged approach.

Laura
Director, Sales Strategy

Hi Elena — looping back with a recommended approach after internal sync.

Recommended staged procurement path for Acme Financial:

1) Short term (0–3 weeks): Subscribe via AWS Marketplace for the hosted Redwood API to expedite onboarding and allow developer teams to start integrating. This satisfies procurement's timeline and provides automated billing through AWS. Marketplace purchase will give you immediate access to our hosted models and standard DPA.

2) Parallel negotiation (3–8 weeks): Begin direct contracting for Dedicated/Private deployment and custom DPA/DPIA edits. This is the path if Acme needs strict data residency guarantees, custom SLAs, or to reserve capacity. We'll surface SOC 2 evidence and work with your legal team on DPA language.

3) Co-sell / Cloud partner support: We'll reach out to the AWS account team to request co-sell engagement; if approved, AWS can help expedite procurement and may enable co-sell incentives. Please let us know the AWS account ID we should reference.

Attachments included for your procurement packet:
- redwood-pricing-worksheet.xlsx (price bands and reserved capacity examples)
- SOC2-sysdesc-excerpt.pdf (controls summary)

Next steps for Acme (simple checklist):
- Confirm whether invoicing via AWS Marketplace is acceptable (if yes, we can proceed immediately).
- If PO/invoice needed instead, confirm billing contact and we will prioritize direct contracting.
- Share AWS account ID if you want us to request co-sell support.

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call with procurement + legal to walk through the options — I'm available Fri 12/3 or Mon 12/6 PST. We'll align to your timezone.

Thanks,
Priyom
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
